_comment: Internal test-quality tool — NOT part of the published package and not
something adopters ever see (no docs page, no handbook section, no emitted
config). It answers one question about THIS repo's own suite: 100% line
coverage says every line ran, not that a wrong line would be caught.
StringLiteral is excluded as a KNOWN GAP, not on evidence. This field used
to claim the exclusion was safe because cutting the cause / next-step half
out of a self-explaining message already turns the suite red. Measured, it
does not: with StringLiteral on, bootstrap/plan.ts drops from 99.42% to
(1 -> 66). The largest group of survivors is the `note` on each planned
action — the line init prints to say what it just did; empty every one of
them and no test fails. Next is the middle sentence of a multi-line
message, where the assertions pin some sentences and not others.
Repo-wide scale is NOT measured yet — do not quote a number for it. The
exclusion stays until the `note` fields and the plugin message texts carry
assertions, and is then re-measured rather than re-assumed.
